skill.name: cocoindex
skill.description: Develop CocoIndex flows for AI data pipelines, including indexing, embedding, extraction, search, live updates, and flow operations.
skill.summary: Build and operate CocoIndex data transformation flows for AI indexing and retrieval.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: No prompt injection or malware intent was found in the skill files. Most static findings are false positives from Markdown formatting, CocoIndex API names, documentation links, and placeholder configuration examples. Confirmed risks remain around credential handling, especially asking users for API key values and printing database URLs during troubleshooting.

remediation.issue: The skill asks users to provide API key values in chat.
remediation.suggestion: Change the guidance to ask users to set local environment variables or secret-manager entries, then confirm only variable names and provider choices.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting guidance can print COCOINDEX_DATABASE_URL from .env.
remediation.suggestion: Replace value-printing commands with presence checks that redact values, and tell users not to paste full connection strings into chat.

remediation.issue: Database URL examples may expose credentials when expanded into command arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer psql service files, local environment loading, or redacted connection tests that avoid showing usernames, passwords, and host details.

remediation.issue: External API examples pass bearer tokens to configurable endpoints.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to validate endpoint ownership, use request timeouts, and never log Authorization headers or API responses containing secrets.

content.value_statement: AI indexing projects need correct flow design, configuration, and operational commands. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code create and manage CocoIndex pipelines with practical examples.
actual_capabilities: Designs CocoIndex flow definitions for local files, cloud sources, databases, and live updates.
Guides embedding, chunking, LLM extraction, vector search, and knowledge graph patterns.
Explains CocoIndex CLI commands for setup, update, evaluate, show, server, and drop workflows.
Helps create custom CocoIndex functions with type annotations, caching, and behavior versions.
Provides troubleshooting guidance for flow targets, schema changes, database setup, and resource limits.
limitations: Requires CocoIndex and related database or vector services to be installed by the user.
Generated examples need review before production use, especially around secrets and network calls.
Cannot verify cloud credentials, database access, or external API quotas without the user environment.
May need newer CocoIndex documentation for features added after the skill was authored.

use_cases.title: Create a Document Search Index
use_cases.description: Build a CocoIndex flow that chunks documents, creates embeddings, and exports searchable vectors to a database.

use_cases.title: Operate Existing Flows
use_cases.description: Run setup, evaluate, update, live update, and inspection commands for CocoIndex projects.

use_cases.title: Prototype AI Knowledge Pipelines
use_cases.description: Combine LLM extraction, custom functions, graph targets, and vector indexes for retrieval workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the CocoIndex skill to create a local document indexing flow. Ask me for the source, target, embedding model, and database settings before writing files.

prompt_templates.title: Add Flow Operations
prompt_templates.scenario: Run and inspect an existing flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the CocoIndex skill to help me run setup, evaluate, update, and show commands for my existing flow. Explain each command before running it.

prompt_templates.title: Design Custom Functions
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the CocoIndex skill to design a cached custom function for enrichment. Use environment variables for secrets and avoid printing secret values.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Production Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the CocoIndex skill to plan a production flow with live updates, vector search, knowledge graph export, concurrency limits, and rollback steps.

output_examples.input: Build a vector search flow for Markdown files.
output_examples.output: A concise flow plan with source selection, chunking strategy, embedding model, target database, setup steps, and validation checks.

output_examples.input: My CocoIndex flow says the database connection failed.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting checklist that checks environment setup, database availability, flow target format, and safe credential handling.

output_examples.input: Add LLM extraction before indexing documents.
output_examples.output: A design outline for a typed custom function, cache behavior, model configuration, and target schema changes.

best_practices: Keep secrets in local environment variables or a secret manager, not in chat or source files.
Use evaluate before update when changing flow logic or target schemas.
Set explicit types, cache versions, and concurrency limits for expensive or high-volume pipelines.
anti_patterns: Do not paste API keys or full database URLs into prompts, logs, or troubleshooting output.
Do not run destructive drop or reset commands without confirming the target flow and environment.
Do not copy examples into production without reviewing access controls, retries, timeouts, and data retention.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps build and operate CocoIndex flows for AI indexing, retrieval, extraction, and data transformation.

faq.question: Does it install CocoIndex automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can suggest dependencies and commands, but the user controls installation and execution.

faq.question: Can it work with vector databases?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes patterns for Postgres with pgvector, Qdrant, LanceDB, and related retrieval workflows.

faq.question: Can it create custom transformations?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains custom function specs, executors, type annotations, caching, and behavior version updates.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Store secrets locally in environment variables or a secret manager. Do not paste secret values into chat.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production systems?
faq.answer: It can help plan production flows, but users must review security, scaling, monitoring, and data governance.
